# **1\. Introduction** {#1.-introduction}

Raffles’ Banded Langurs is one of Singapore’s critically endangered species, with a limited population of around 67 individuals. It faces a significant threat to its long-term survival from 2 main areas. The lack of public attention due to its elusive and arboreal nature, and also the misidentification of RBLs with other species which may share some of the same characteristics. The protection of RBLs stands as a priority for Singapore’s wildlife and conservation efforts. 

To address these challenges, the Raffles’ Banded Langur Working Group (RBLWG) established a community based citizen science programme that engages with the general public in monitoring and reporting sightings of RBLs. Through volunteer participation in regular survey walks, it aims to promote awareness of RBLs and also gather information that can be used to support research and future conservation efforts. 

## **1.1 Purpose** {#1.1-purpose}

The system is intended to support the activities of citizen science volunteers, researchers and organisers who are involved within the data collection, management and use of RBL sighting data. 

The system aims to address the limitations of the current data collection process. RBLWG has been using two *Google Sheets* documents to keep track of both volunteer data and the sightings they record. While the method has been in use for several cycles, Volunteers and organisers have reported challenges when using the old format. Problems may include fragmented data entry, limited ease of use in field conditions, and lack of coordination possibility.

Our group aims to develop an application to assist RBLWG and its volunteers in addressing these challenges and improving the overall workflow. The system is intended to centralise data collection, improve volunteer and organiser coordination, and support a consistent recording of sighting information that is reliable and readily available for future analysis or usage. 

This is a multifaceted ideal, with goals surrounding automating administrative aspects such as survey bookings and follow-up communication, facilitating data collection, volunteer collaboration and communication and more.

## **1.2 Scope** {#1.2-scope}

The main scope of this system is to support and streamline the workflow of both by members of the RBLWG along with volunteers from the general public (citizen scientists). By providing a centralised application for survey coordination and sighting data submission. This system is intended to replace the existing  Google Sheets workflow with a more smooth and structured workflow whilst providing a similar if not higher degree of base functionality. 

It must also fulfill several additional features outlined by RBLWG in the system, mentioned below. 

Finally, it’s also important that this system is planned, architectured, built, tested and deployed correctly in order to best help the RBLWG reach their conservation goals, and to maintain the sustainability of the system far into the future, given the group’s long-term goals.

Our core **user groups** include: 

* Survey walk volunteers (citizen scientists), and  
* Dr Andie, or a general organizer role

Our system **will** **allow survey walk volunteers to:**

* Create, view, update and delete survey walk bookings   
* View other bookings associated within the same survey walk / route slot  
* Record sightings of RBLs and other species as a group leader, which includes:  
  * Submit details (time, location, species type) in text form  
  * Submit photos and videos, during and after expeditions  
  * Record location of sightings using GPS data  
* Visualize sighting data from prior survey walks  
* Invite volunteers to join the same survey walk   
* Learn how to use the application through tutorials  
* View emergency hotlines in cases of incidents

Furthermore, it **will also allow the organiser to:**

* Create, view, update, delete survey periods  
* Create, view, update, delete survey walks in a certain period  
* Notify volunteers when the survey dates are approaching (via email)  
* Notify volunteers when a survey walk has been cancelled  
* Notify volunteers of any route changes, such as blockages or weather-related issues  
* Notify volunteers when they are not reaching the survey walk quota  
* Notify volunteers when they did not attend a booked survey walk  
* View several statistics about past few survey walks  
  * No. of groups / week  
  * Attendance rate  
  * Quota completion rate  
* Export to another format (Google Sheet, Excel, or CSV file)

It will also:

* Authenticate users   
* Work offline with saved drafts  
* Accommodate for accessibility options

Our web applications **will not**:

* Include extensive gamification elements, e.g. intrusive levelling systems, leaderboards, etc. Any minor gamification elements will be easily toggleable.  
* Allow volunteers to see sighting data from survey walks that they did not attend.  
* Allow volunteers to view broader statistics about other survey walks.  
* Allow volunteers to create/manage their own survey walks.

## **1.3 Definitions, Acronyms, and Abbreviations** {#1.3-definitions,-acronyms,-and-abbreviations}

* RBL: Raffles’ Banded Langur, a primate species in Singapore  
* RBLWG: Raffles’ Banded Langur Working Group: a mutli-organization group dedicated to the conservation and study of RBLs.  
* Survey walks: Programmes conducted by the RBLWG where members of the general public travel along a forest trail to spot RBLSs as well as other forest species, which also aims to collect data on RBLs in the forest region.  
* Volunteer / Survey Walk Volunteer: A general term describing members of the general public who attend survey walks conducted by RBLWG, separate from those organizing them.  
* Citizen science: Research conducted with participation from the general public or non-professional researchers.  
* Organiser: Dr Andie Ang, or a member of RBLWG who has administrative access to manage survey periods and survey walks  
* PDPA: Personal Data Protection Act, a law in Singapore that details standards for protection of personal data.  
* XLSX: Extensible file-sheet format, commonly used in Microsoft Excel and Google Sheets  
* OAuth2: An open protocol for authorisation, developed by the IETF (Internet Engineering Task Force)

# **2\. Overall Description** {#2.-overall-description}

## **2.1 Product Perspective** {#2.1-product-perspective}

The product is a web application that ideally replaces the Google Sheets that RBLWG has been utilizing for past survey walks. It acts as a bridge or connection between user and organizer, and also provides useful functions to the users and lets the organizer collect the data more conveniently.

The application will act as a standalone system that interacts with several external services. Its two main user groups will interact with said system, and certain operations will cause the system to interact with either an email service, a database service, or both. Ideally, the database service should not be facing any user group, and the email service will only interact with the user through emails sent.

![][image1]

Context Diagram for our planned system

## **2.2 User Characteristics** {#2.2-user-characteristics}

* **Persona 1: Experienced Volunteer (e.g., "Alex")**  
  * Background*:* A nature enthusiast who participates in field observations.  
  * Technical Expertise: Proficient with mobile devices but requires a simple, intuitive interface for data entry in outdoor settings.  
  * Needs: Easy GPS tagging, quick photo/data uploads, and the ability to communicate with other volunteers.

* **Persona 2: New Volunteer (e.g. “Alice”)**  
  * Background: A casual nature enthusiast who is interested in conservation but rarely participates in citizen science projects.  
  * Technical Expertise: Proficient with mobile devices but not knowledgeable of platforms often used for citizen science projects.  
  * Needs: Some amount of in app guidance and clear instructions of how to use the application and how to conduct survey walks in general.

* **Persona 3: A group of volunteers (e.g. “Bob”, “William”, “Chris”)**  
  * Background: A group of nature-loving friends participating in a citizen science project together.  
  * Technical Expertise: Proficient with mobile devices; however, they require a group upload feature.  
  * Needs: Data should only need to be uploaded by one representative on behalf of the entire group.

* **Persona 4: Organizer (e.g., "Dr. Tan")**  
  * Background: A researcher responsible for coordinating conservation efforts and analyzing data.  
  * Technical Expertise: Comfortable with data management tools and administrative interfaces.  
  * Needs: Centralized data access, ability to notify all volunteers about tasks, and tools to visualize observation trends.

## **2.3 Constraints** {#2.3-constraints}

* Hardware Requirements

As our application is designed to be used by a wide variety of devices (desktop and mobile), our application needs to be able to function on a generally wide range of screen sizes. Furthermore, it must also fully support both keyboard/mouse based input, as well as touch input. 

* Software Requirements

Given the scope of the project, our application will focus on a progressive web application to be developed first and foremost. While a native mobile app will maximize usability for mobile users, it will be a secondary priority and will be done on a best-effort basis. The application must support usage with screen readers and other accessibility tools, to ensure volunteers with any impairments or disabilities are able to use the application.

* Data Protection Requirements

As our application is developed and designed to be used in Singapore, it must adhere to the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) (Personal Data Protection Commission, 2023). In particular, the most crucial obligations that our team would need to consider for our context include:

* Notification obligation  
* Consent obligation  
* Accuracy obligation  
* Protection obligation  
* Access and Correction obligation  
* Data Portability Obligation  
* Data Breach Notification Obligation

Other obligations may also be factored in as development progresses.

## **2.4 Assumptions and Dependencies** {#2.4-assumptions-and-dependencies}

Assumptions

**Device Availability**: It is assumed that volunteers have access to an internet-enabled device (mobile phone or laptop), and can access web applications before/after the survey walks.

**Digital Proficiency**: It is assumed that all registered volunteers, regardless of age, possess a baseline level of digital literacy, enabling them to navigate mobile or desktop web interfaces, and perform basic data entry without intensive technical support. 

**No Duplicates of Sighting Records:** It is assumed that the group leader will not create duplicate sightings on behalf of the group, i.e. all submitted records are accurate and thus little need is present to allow modifiability.

Dependencies

**External Email Service:** Our choice of email service must be reliable enough to handle batch jobs of sending tens to hundreds of emails at once, given the considered organiser role.

**Database Service:** Our choice of database service must be reliable enough to handle at least tens of read/write operations at once, given the number of people who can access the system during the same survey walk.

**Authentication Service:** Our choice of an authentication service (if any) must be secure, reliable, and fast enough to minimize disruptions to the workflow as well as keep our users’ data secure.

# **3\. Requirements Analysis** {#3.-requirements-analysis}

Our requirements include both functional and non-functional requirements as detailed below:

## **3.1 Functional Requirements** {#3.1-functional-requirements}

### **3.1.1 User Requirements** {#3.1.1-user-requirements}

**UR-1:** The system should allow users to login, sign-up using their credentials.

**UR-2:** The system shall allow users to create, manage, and delete survey walk bookings within the application.

**UR-3:** The system shall allow users to view the survey walk bookings made by other members of their designated group.

**UR-4:** The system shall allow users to invite other members to join their booking for the same survey walk.

**UR-5:** The system shall automatically notify users via email when a scheduled survey walk appointment is approaching, or when an appointment has been cancelled.

**UR-6:** The system shall allow volunteers to submit photos and langur sighting records both during and after an expedition.

**UR-7:** The system shall provide a mechanism to coordinate group submissions to prevent the entry of duplicate sighting data for the same observation. This will involve one group member being selected as the “leader”, with the ability to modify and delete duplicate submissions on behalf of the group.

**UR-8:** The system shall capture the device's GPS coordinates once the user triggers the recording action, or allow them to input a rough location manually if GPS is unavailable.

**UR-9:** The system shall allow organizers to export all collected observation data directly into the existing Google Sheets format. 

**UR-10:** The system shall support recording sightings of non-langur species using dynamic data entry boxes that change based on the selected species.

**UR-11:** The system shall allow volunteers to record observations offline in areas with poor cellular service and save them as a draft until they can submit it once connection is restored.

**UR-12:** The system shall provide data visualization results with a user-controlled toggle, allowing users to choose whether these features are displayed based on their personal preference.

**UR-13:** The system shall include an integrated tutorial to guide users through the application's functions and general usage.

**UR-14:** The system will automatically check the weather forecast before any scheduled walks, and notify volunteers if the weather is likely to be non-conducive or dangerous (i.e. lightning).

#### **2\. Important Use Cases** {#2.-important-use-cases}

UC0A \- Register

Actor: Volunteer

Postconditions: User verification request is made

Normal Flow:

1. The volunteer chooses to register to the system.  
2. The system directs the user to register through an external authentication service (e.g. through OAuth2).  
3. The volunteer enters the requested details in 2\.  
4. The system receives confirmation from the authentication service.

5. The system indicates that the verification request has been made.

Exceptions:

5a. System detects that entered details are incorrect (E1)

	5a1. The system shows an error message to the user.

	5a2. The system disables further submission until details are changed.

	Use case resumes at step 2\.

UC0B \- Verify User

Actor: Organizer

Preconditions: User is logged in as an organizer

Postconditions: Volunteer can login to the system

Normal Flow:

1. The organizer chooses to verify a user.  
2. The system displays the list of users pending verification.  
3. The organizer selects a specific user to verify.  
4. The system marks the user as verified.

UC01 \- Login

Actor: Volunteer or Organizer (User)

Postconditions: User is logged in and the current session is stored.

Normal Flow:

1. The user chooses to login to the system.  
2. The system requests for username and password.  
3. The system also shows the option to login through an external authentication service.  
4. The user enters the requested details in 2\.  
5. The system verifies the requested details.  
6. The system displays the system’s functionalities.

Alternative Flows:

3a. The user chooses to login through an external authentication service.

	3a1. The system receives confirmation from the authentication service.

	Use case resumes from step 6\.

Exceptions:

5a. The user is not verified yet.

	5a1. The system indicates that the user is yet to be verified.

Other exceptions: E1

UC02 \- Create Booking

Actor: Volunteer

Preconditions: User is logged in and verified

Normal Flow:

1.   The volunteer chooses to create a booking for a survey walk.  
2.   System displays available survey walks for booking.  
3.   The volunteer selects a specific survey walk to book.  
4.   System requests for confirmation.  
5.   User confirms.  
6.   System registers volunteer for survey walks.

Alternative Flows:

5a. System fails to register volunteer due to reaching capacity

	5a1. System displays error message

	5a2. User dismisses message

	5a3. System refreshes list of available survey walks

	Use case resumes from step 4\.

6a. User is first to book the survey walk

	6a1. User is automatically assigned as group leader

UC03 \- Delete Booking

Actor: Volunteer

Preconditions: User is logged in and verified, User has at least on existing booking for a survey walk

Normal Flow:

1. Volunteers chooses to view their current bookings  
2. System displays a list of upcoming events  
3. Volunteer selects a booking to delete	  
4. System requires confirmation  
5. Volunteer confirms deletion  
6. System removes the volunteer from the survey walk  
7. System updates survey availability  
8. Other members are informed of the cancellation

Alternative flows:

4a. User cancels the action (A1)

	4a1. System returns to prior page that user visited

	4a2. No changes made

UC04 \- Record Sighting

Actor: Volunteer

Preconditions: User is logged in and verified, User has an active or completed survey walk booking, User is group leader

Normal Flow:

1. The volunteer selects “Record Sighting” during or after a survey walk  
2. System displays sighting input form  
3. Volunteer enter sighting details  
4. Volunteer completes form details  
5. Volunteer submits sighting  
6. System validates and stores the sighting  
7. System confirms submission

Alternative Flows:

3a. Required fields missing

	3a1. System displays an error, highlights missing fields

	3a2. User can save current data as a draft or try again

	Use case resumes from step 3\.

5a. Volunteer chooses to save a draft first

	5a1. Volunteer selects option to save data as a draft first

	5a2. System saves any data onto a draft saved locally

	5a3. Volunteer chooses to submit a draft

	5a4. System shows list of drafts, indicating their completion status

	5a5. Volunteer selects a draft

Use case resumes from step 5

6a. Submission fails due to internal server error (E2)

	6a1. System displays error

	6a2. User can save current data as a draft or try again

	Use case resumes from step 6\.

![][image3]

*Example of how a UI for recording sighting data could look*

UC05 \- View Sighting Data

Actor: Volunteer

Preconditions: User is logged in and is verified

Normal Flow:

1. Volunteer selects the option to view sighting data  
2. System displays a table / map of recorded sightings  
3. Volunteer applies filters  
4. Volunteer selects sighting  
5. System displays information about sighting

Exceptions: E2

UC06 \- Create survey period

Actor: Organizer

Preconditions: User is logged in as organizer  
Normal Flow:

1. Administrator chooses to create a new survey period  
2. System prompts for survey period details  
3. Admin enters required information  
4. Admin confirms creation  
5. System creates the survey period

Exceptions: E1, E2

Alternative Flows: A1

UC07 \- Create survey walk

Actor: Organizer

Preconditions: User is logged in as organizer  
Normal Flow:

1. Administrator selects the survey period  
2. Administrator chooses to create a new survey walk  
3. System prompts for survey walk details  
4. Admin enters required information  
5. Admin confirms creation  
6. System creates the survey walk

Exceptions: E1, E2

UC08 \- See statistics

Actor: Organizer

Preconditions: User is logged in as organizer  
Normal Flow:

1. The organizer selects the "Statistics" module from the dashboard.  
2. The system displays a list of available statistical categories (e.g., Volunteer Participation, Survey Progress).  
3. The organizer chooses to view statistics for the "past few survey walks."  
4. System calculates and displays the following data:  
   1. No. of groups / week (Visualized as a trend chart).  
   2. Attendance rate (Comparison between registered and actual attendees).  
   3. Quota fulfilling rate (Progress towards the target number of surveys).  
5. The organizer filters or exports the data if necessary.

Exceptions: E2

UC09 \- See statistics

Actor: Volunteer

Preconditions: User is logged in and verified  
Normal Flow:

1. Volunteer navigates to the "My Statistics" or "Contribution" page.  
2. Volunteer chooses whether the visualization statistics will appear (Toggle "On/Off").  
3. System prompts for the specific survey period or "History" view.  
4. System displays personal survey walk outcomes, including:  
   1. Sighting record: Total number of Raffles' Banded Langurs encountered.  
   2. Walk history: Summary of completed vs. missed walks.  
   3. Observation details: Specific locations where langurs were spotted.  
5. The volunteer views their contribution to the overall citizen science project.

Exceptions: E2

UC10 \- Export data to file

Actor: Organizer

Preconditions: User is logged in as organizer  
Normal Flow:

1. Organizer chooses to export all survey walk data into a file  
2. System asks for confirmation  
3. Organizer confirms choice to export  
4. System starts processing data, packaging it into an XLSX file  
5. System displays loading indicator while it is processing data  
6. System sends XLSX file to the organizer  
7. Organizer opens the file from their downloaded files folder

Exceptions: E2

Alternative Flows: A1

UC11 \- Notify volunteers

Actor: Organizer

Preconditions: User is logged in as organizer  
Normal Flow:

1. The organizer chooses to notify volunteers about a certain topic.  
2. System displays options to notify either   
   1. those about to attend a survey walk in the next 24 hours,   
   2. those who missed a survey walk they already booked,  
   3. those who are are likely to miss their period completion quota, or  
   4. other, where the organizer specifies on their own  
3. Organizer enters in details, i.e. the message and people to email  
4. Organizer chooses to submit the notification order  
5. System asks for confirmation from the organizer  
6. Organizer confirms the action  
7. System processes the emails and/or in-app notification order and sends them out to relevant users  
8. System displays loading indicator while notifications are sent out  
9. System shows success message once notifications are all sent

Exceptions: E1, E2

Alternative Flows: A1

## **3.2 Non-Functional Requirements** {#3.2-non-functional-requirements}

* Reliability/Availability

System uptime must be no less than 95%. A high system uptime is important because the system must be usable at most times for users to manage their bookings and organizers to do general administrative tasks. We note that 95% is significantly less than the uptime goals of most SaaS products, however it’s still a reasonable target for our users (especially if they don’t require access 24/7).

* Usability (UI/UX) and Responsiveness

The system shall feature an intuitive interface designed for speed and ease of use, ensuring volunteers can record sightings quickly and with minimal effort (within two clicks/taps). It must provide immediate feedback for all user actions within 200ms, maintaining a seamless experience. Because the system will be used on devices outdoors, the interface must be legible in bright sunlight. This means using large font sizes and contrasting UI elements.

* Security / Data Confidentiality

The system shall ensure that all user credentials and sensitive sighting coordinates are encrypted and securely stored. Access controls must be implemented so that personal information is only accessible to authorized organizers, protecting the privacy of volunteers and the integrity of the research data.

* Performance

The system must run efficiently on end users’ devices, with regards to usability and avoiding frustration for users. It should also aim to avoid unnecessary computation/GPS lookups, in order to preserve battery life on mobile devices. 

* Scalability / Modifiability

The system shall be designed with a modular architecture to easily accommodate an increasing number of volunteers and new types of walks, locations or target species. This flexibility ensures that developers can update features or expand database capacity as the citizen science project grows over time. This also means the system will be as maintainable as possible for potential future developers, when the system requires maintenance.

## **3.3 Data Requirements** {#3.3-data-requirements}

Our data field will be roughly organized based on the ER diagram below. The Optional values are, as expected, not required for the behavior of the system. In the case of a Sighting however, the more data available the better. The volunteer quota is set by Dr Andie, and allows her to view volunteers that aren’t contributing to the project.

Volunteers may be able to choose to “gameify” their account, in which case they will gain EXP and be able to see other game features, with the goal of making expeditions more motivating. This features will be designed to be very minimal, and not impact the functionality or usability of the app.

This data is a superset of the data stored in the Google Sheet, as we need to ensure we at least match its functionality.
